question: A warehouse had 204 boxes initially. They removed 41 boxes for shipment. They added 15 boxes from returns. They multiplied by 9 to track total inventory. They removed 223 boxes for a big order. They removed 911 boxes for a bulk sale. They removed 63 more boxes for warehouse closure. How many boxes were left?

A store started with 20 items in stock. They added 37 items from morning delivery. They removed 23 items sold to customers. They added 41 items from afternoon shipment. They multiplied by 6 for the month's projection. Michael had twice as many items and Sarah had the standard count. How many items were expected?

A farm had 134 chickens initially. They removed 124 chickens for harvest. They added 8 chickens from new breeding. They multiplied by 3 to calculate egg production. They tripled again for the quarterly forecast. There were 156 ducks (not counted). How many chickens were in the annual projection?

A school added 219 students gradually. They added 5 students in week one. They added 39 more students in week two. They added 38 students in week three. They removed 12 students for transfers. They multiplied by 9 for the semester capacity. How many student-seats were needed?

A factory started with 66 units. They tripled production in the morning. They tripled again in the afternoon. They added 7 units from repairs. They added 57 more units from a new line. How many units were produced in total?

A business had 93 customers initially. They added 40 customers from marketing. They added 4 customers from referrals. They added 80 more customers from a sale. They added 33 customers from partnerships. How many total customers did they have?

A farmer had 232 apples. They added 43 apples from morning harvest. They added 11 more apples from the orchard. They removed 161 apples for market sale. They multiplied remaining by 6 for juice production. How many apples would make juice?

A workshop started with 91 tools. They removed 3 tools for sharpening. They multiplied remaining by 7 for the project. They multiplied by 8 for the team calculation. They added 11 tools from new delivery. There were 24 power tools in storage. How many tools were available in total?

A school started with 13 students initially. They added 21 students in morning class. They added 57 more students in afternoon. They added 80 students in evening session. They added another 80 students in the summer program. They removed 135 students for graduations. How many students remained enrolled?

A warehouse had 198 items. They added 27 items from morning shipment. They multiplied by 8 for the annual value. They tripled to calculate replacement cost. They added 39 items from audit findings. The damaged section had 16 items (not counted). How much was the replacement value calculation?

A factory started with 201 units. They added 28 units from morning production. They added 29 more units from afternoon. They added 40 units from the evening shift. They multiplied by 3 for daily target planning. They removed 104 units for quality checks. How many units met quality standards?

A store had 179 products. They added 72 products from delivery. They removed 133 products for restocking. They multiplied by 7 for inventory projection. They doubled for the monthly count. There were 45 special items not counted. How many products were projected?

A contractor had 220 materials initially. They removed 166 materials for the first job. They multiplied by 7 for seven different projects. They added 73 materials from new delivery. They multiplied by 7 again for the season. How many materials were needed for the season?

A library had 153 books initially. They added 57 books from donation. They multiplied by 6 to calculate total value. They added 50 more books from another donor. They multiplied by 6 again for insurance. They added 47 books from library sale. They added 15 books from inheritance. How many books was the insurance calculation?

A company started with 140 projects. They added 5 projects in week one. They added 74 projects in week two. They multiplied by 8 to calculate total person-hours. They added 71 from consultant hours. They removed 1108 hours for vacation time. How many billable hours remained?

A gardener had 199 plants. They multiplied by 5 for the growth rate calculation. They added 16 plants from cuttings. They added 6 more plants from seeds. They added 57 plants from a nursery. They doubled for the seasonal forecast. There were 23 plants in the greenhouse. How many plants were in the seasonal forecast?

A school had 136 desks initially. They multiplied by 7 for classroom setup. They multiplied by 5 for the building layout. They added 9 additional desks. They added 45 more desks from donation. How many desks were available in total?

A warehouse had 83 boxes. They multiplied by 9 to track item count. They added 36 items from new shipment. They divided by 3 to split into sections. They added 70 items to each section. They removed 154 items for delivery. How many items were delivered?

A store started with 217 items. They added 55 items in the morning. They added 67 items in the afternoon. They multiplied by 4 to calculate daily value. They divided by 2 for two store locations. They divided by 2 again for inventory split. They added 63 items to each location. How many items were in the final inventory?

A company had 114 employees. They removed 81 employees due to reorganization. They added 64 employees from merger. They multiplied by 6 to calculate total compensation. They added 68 employees from expansion. How many employees were there after expansion?

A library had 203 books initially. They removed 76 books for archiving. They removed 5 books that were lost. They removed 51 more books for donation. They multiplied by 5 to calculate catalog value. How many dollars was the catalog value?

A child had 23 toys initially. They added 19 toys for their birthday. They removed 18 toys that were broken. They multiplied by 2 to account for duplicates. They multiplied by 4 for storage planning. They added 73 toys from an older sibling. How many toys were in the collection?

A musician had 67 sheet music pieces. They removed 49 pieces from the old repertoire. They divided by 3 to organize by difficulty. They added 80 pieces from new compositions. They added 56 pieces from a collection. They added 7 more pieces from practice materials. How many pieces were in the final repertoire?

A store started with 26 items. They removed 1 item from damaged stock. They multiplied by 7 for seven locations. They added 23 items to each location. They doubled for the extended hours. They removed 323 items for a closing sale. How many items were left after the sale?

A warehouse had 174 boxes. They added 80 boxes from morning delivery. They removed 105 boxes for shipment. They added 15 boxes from returns. They doubled the remaining inventory. They doubled again for the storage forecast. How many storage units were needed?
